**Finding submitted: deviation (medium severity, fallback redline).**

**What I found**
- **No minimum purchase commitment.** Section 3.1 fees are a pure revenue share (30% of monthly Net Sales above $11,000), with no minimum spend, guaranteed volume, or shortfall mechanic. Section 6.1 restricts us competitively (exclusivity), but that is not a volume cap and falls outside this rule.
- **But Section 4.2(a) is a take-or-pay proxy on exit.** Our only exit under Section 4.1 is 90 days' notice; exercising it triggers a payment equal to half of trailing 12-month Net Sales less $800,000, payable in eight quarterly installments. It is volume-based, one-directional (only when *we* terminate), and applies even if we terminate because HDI failed to perform — a penalty rather than a true-up.

**Position taken**
Preferred (delete the payment) is disproportionate here: HDI bears all design, development, hosting and promotion costs (Sections 1.2, 1.6, 1.8) with no fixed fees from us, so the payment is a negotiated recoupment. I took the fallback with a single minimal insertion into Section 4.2(a) carving out (i) termination for HDI's material breach and (ii) termination under Section 1.6 — which already promises termination "without penalty," so that carve-out simply removes an internal inconsistency.
